sentences.zh: 志七十六

translations.literal: Treatise 76
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 76

sentences.zh: 樂八

translations.literal: Music 8
translations.idiomatic: Music 8

sentences.zh: 清代樂制，有中和韶樂、丹陛大樂、中和清樂、丹陛清樂、導迎樂、鐃歌樂、禾辭桑歌樂、慶神歡樂、宴樂、賜宴樂、鄉樂，器則隨所用而各異，悉依樂部次第，臚列而備舉之。

translations.literal: The Qing dynasty music system has Zhonghe Shao Music, Danbi Grand Music, Zhonghe Qing Music, Danbi Qing Music, Processional Welcome Music, Nao Song Music, Grain Ode and Mulberry Song Music, Joyous Celebration of the Spirits Music, Banquet Music, Imperial Gift Banquet Music, and Village Music; the instruments differ according to each use, and all are set forth in full enumeration following the Music Bureau's order.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing music system comprised Zhonghe Shao Music, Danbi Grand Music, Zhonghe Qing Music, Danbi Qing Music, processional welcome music, nao song music, grain-ode and mulberry-song music, joyous spirit-celebration music, banquet music, imperial gift-banquet music, and village music. Instruments varied with each occasion; all are recorded here in the order prescribed by the Music Bureau, item by item.

sentences.zh: 所獲籓屬樂器，列於宴樂，古所未詳，尤不可略。

translations.literal: Musical instruments obtained from dependent domains are listed under banquet music; ancient texts had never described them in detail, and they especially must not be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments received from tributary domains appear under banquet music—a category never fully documented in antiquity and not to be passed over lightly.

sentences.zh: 然第志其名稱形制而已，若夫尺度聲律，則有司存。

translations.literal: However, this only records their names and forms; as for dimensions and pitch standards, the responsible officials maintain those records.
translations.idiomatic: Here only names and forms are recorded; questions of measurement and pitch regulation belong to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 中和韶樂，用於壇、廟者，鎛鍾一，特磬一，編鐘十六，編磬十六，建鼓一，篪六，排簫二，塤二，簫十，笛十，琴十，瑟四，笙十，搏拊二，柷一，敔一，麾一。

translations.literal: For altars and temples, Zhonghe Shao Music employs one bo bell, one solo chime set, sixteen serial bells, sixteen serial chimes, one set-up drum, six chi flutes, two panpipes, two xun ocarinas, ten xiao flutes, ten di flutes, ten qin zithers, four se zithers, ten sheng mouth-organs, two hand clappers, one zhù sounding-block, one yù wooden tiger, and one conductor's baton.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe Shao Music for altars and temples calls for one bo bell, one solo chime set, sixteen serial bells and sixteen serial chimes, one set-up drum, six chi, two panpipes, two xun, ten xiao, ten di, ten qin, four se, ten sheng, two hand-clappers, a zhù, a yù, and a conductor's baton.

sentences.zh: 先師廟，琴、簫、笛、笙各六，篪四，餘同。

translations.literal: At the Temple of the Former Master, qin, xiao, di, and sheng are six each, chi four; the rest the same.
translations.idiomatic: At the Temple of the Former Master, there are six each of qin, xiao, di, and sheng, four chi, and the remainder as above.

sentences.zh: 巡幸祭方岳，不用鎛鍾、特磬，琴、簫、笛、笙各四，瑟、篪各二，餘同。

translations.literal: When the emperor tours and sacrifices at the sacred mountains, bo bells and solo chimes are not used; qin, xiao, di, and sheng are four each, se and chi two each; the rest the same.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours when sacrificing at the sacred mountains, bo bells and solo chimes are omitted; qin, xiao, di, and sheng are four each, se and chi two each, and the remainder as above.

sentences.zh: 用於殿陛者，簫四，笛四，篪二，琴四，瑟二，笙八，餘同。

translations.literal: When used on palace hall steps, xiao four, di four, chi two, qin four, se two, sheng eight; the rest the same.
translations.idiomatic: For use on palace hall steps, there are four xiao, four di, two chi, four qin, two se, eight sheng, and the remainder as above.

sentences.zh: 鎛鍾，範金為之，凡十二，應十二律。

translations.literal: Bo bells are cast from metal; twelve in all, corresponding to the twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Bo bells are cast in metal—twelve in all, one for each of the twelve pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 其制皆上徑小，下徑大，縱徑大，橫徑小。

translations.literal: Their form is uniformly small in upper diameter and large in lower diameter, large in vertical diameter and small in horizontal diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Each is shaped with a smaller upper rim and larger lower rim, greater in vertical than in horizontal diameter.

sentences.zh: 乳三十六。

translations.literal: Thirty-six nipple-bosses.
translations.idiomatic: They bear thirty-six nipple-bosses.

sentences.zh: 兩角下垂。

translations.literal: Two corners droop downward.
translations.idiomatic: The two corners hang down.

sentences.zh: 十二鍾各虡，大小異制。

translations.literal: Each of the twelve bells has its own frame; sizes differ in construction.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve bells stands on its own frame, and the frames vary in size.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之鐘，兩欒高一尺八寸二分二釐，甬長一尺零八分，以次遞減至應鍾之鐘，兩欒高九寸六分，甬長五寸六分八釐。

translations.literal: The Huangzhong bell: both crowns one chi eight cun two fen two li in height, shank one chi zero cun eight fen in length; decreasing in succession to the Yingzhong bell, both crowns nine cun six fen in height, shank five cun six fen eight li in length.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangzhong bell stands one chi, eight cun, two fen, and two li between its crowns, with a shank one chi and eight fen long; sizes decrease step by step to the Yingzhong bell, whose crowns measure nine cun and six fen and whose shank is five cun, six fen, and eight li.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之鐘，十一月用之；

translations.literal: The Huangzhong bell is used in the eleventh month;
translations.idiomatic: The Huangzhong bell is used in the eleventh month;

sentences.zh: 大呂之鐘，十二月用之；

translations.literal: The Dalü bell is used in the twelfth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Dalü bell is used in the twelfth month;

sentences.zh: 太簇之鐘，正月用之；

translations.literal: The Taicu bell is used in the first month;
translations.idiomatic: The Taicu bell is used in the first month;

sentences.zh: 夾鍾之鐘，二月用之；

translations.literal: The Jiazhong bell is used in the second month;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiazhong bell is used in the second month;

sentences.zh: 姑洗之鐘，三月用之；

translations.literal: The Guxi bell is used in the third month;
translations.idiomatic: The Guxi bell is used in the third month;

sentences.zh: 仲呂之鐘，四月用之；

translations.literal: The Zhonglü bell is used in the fourth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhonglü bell is used in the fourth month;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之鐘，五月用之；

translations.literal: The Ruibin bell is used in the fifth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Ruibin bell is used in the fifth month;

sentences.zh: 林鍾之鐘，六月用之；

translations.literal: The Linzhong bell is used in the sixth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Linzhong bell is used in the sixth month;

sentences.zh: 夷則之鐘，七月用之；

translations.literal: The Yize bell is used in the seventh month;
translations.idiomatic: The Yize bell is used in the seventh month;

sentences.zh: 南呂之鐘，八月用之；

translations.literal: The Nanlü bell is used in the eighth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Nanlü bell is used in the eighth month;

sentences.zh: 無射之鐘，九月用之；

translations.literal: The Wushe bell is used in the ninth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Wushe bell is used in the ninth month;

sentences.zh: 應鍾之鐘，十月用之。

translations.literal: The Yingzhong bell is used in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhong bell is used in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 鍾之簨虡凡四，皆塗金、上簨左右刻龍首，脊樹金鸞，咮銜五采流蘇，龍口亦如之，下垂至趺。

translations.literal: The bell frames number four in all; all are gilded; the upper crossbars are carved with dragon heads left and right; on the ridge stands a golden luan bird whose beak holds five-colored tassels, and the dragon mouths likewise, hanging down to the base.
translations.idiomatic: There are four bell frames in all, each gilded. Dragon heads are carved at either end of the upper crossbar; a golden luan bird stands on the ridge, its beak holding five-colored tassels, and the dragon mouths hold the same, trailing down to the base.

sentences.zh: 中簨有業，鏤雲龍。

translations.literal: The middle crossbar has a mounting plate, engraved with cloud-and-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The middle crossbar bears a mounting plate engraved with cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 附簨結黃絨紃以懸鐘。

translations.literal: Attached to the crossbar, yellow velvet cords are tied to suspend the bell.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow velvet cords are tied to the crossbar to suspend the bell.

sentences.zh: 左右兩虡，承以五采伏獅。

translations.literal: The two frames left and right are supported by five-colored crouching lions.
translations.idiomatic: The two side frames rest on five-colored crouching lions.

sentences.zh: 下為趺，趺上有垣，鏤山水形。

translations.literal: Below is the base; on the base is a parapet engraved in the form of mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath them is a base topped by a parapet engraved with mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾、大呂、太簇三虡尺度同，夾鍾、姑洗、仲呂三虡尺度同，蕤賓、林鍾、夷則三虡尺度同，南呂、無射、應鍾三虡尺度同，用時不並陳，如以黃鍾為宮，則祗懸黃鍾之鐘。

translations.literal: The Huangzhong, Dalü, and Taicu frames share the same dimensions; Jiazhong, Guxi, and Zhonglü frames share the same dimensions; Ruibin, Linzhong, and Yize frames share the same dimensions; Nanlü, Wushe, and Yingzhong frames share the same dimensions. When in use they are not displayed together; if Huangzhong serves as the tonic, only the Huangzhong bell is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The frames for Huangzhong, Dalü, and Taicu are one size; those for Jiazhong, Guxi, and Zhonglü another; Ruibin, Linzhong, and Yize a third; and Nanlü, Wushe, and Yingzhong a fourth. They are never displayed all at once—when Huangzhong serves as the tonic, only the Huangzhong bell is hung.

sentences.zh: 餘月仿此。

translations.literal: The remaining months follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Other months follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 特磬，以和闐玉為之，凡十二，應十二律。

translations.literal: Solo chimes are made of Khotan jade; twelve in all, corresponding to the twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Solo chimes are fashioned from Khotan jade—twelve in all, matching the twelve pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 其制為鈍角矩形，長股謂之鼓，短股謂之股，皆兩面為雲龍形，穿孔系紃而懸之。

translations.literal: Their form is a blunt-cornered rectangle; the longer leg is called the drum, the shorter leg the thigh; both faces are shaped as cloud-and-dragon patterns, with holes pierced through which cords are threaded for suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Each is a blunt-cornered rectangle: the longer side is called the drum, the shorter the thigh. Both faces bear cloud-and-dragon designs, and holes are pierced for suspension cords.

sentences.zh: 十二磬各虡，大小異制。

translations.literal: Each of the twelve chimes has its own frame; sizes differ in construction.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve chimes has its own frame, and the frames vary in size.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之磬，股長一尺四寸五分八釐，鼓長二尺一寸八分七釐。

translations.literal: The Huangzhong chime: thigh one chi four cun five fen eight li in length, drum two chi one cun eight fen seven li in length.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangzhong chime measures one chi, four cun, five fen, and eight li along the thigh and two chi, one cun, eight fen, and seven li along the drum.

sentences.zh: 以次遞減，至應鍾之磬，股長七寸六分八釐，鼓長一尺一寸五分二釐。

translations.literal: Decreasing in succession to the Yingzhong chime: thigh seven cun six fen eight li in length, drum one chi one cun five fen two li in length.
translations.idiomatic: Sizes decrease step by step to the Yingzhong chime, whose thigh is seven cun, six fen, and eight li and whose drum is one chi, one cun, five fen, and two li.

sentences.zh: 愈小者質愈厚，黃鍾之磬，厚七分二釐九豪，遞增至應鍾之磬，厚一寸二分九釐六豪。

translations.literal: The smaller the chime, the thicker the material; the Huangzhong chime is seven fen two li nine hao thick, increasing in succession to the Yingzhong chime at one cun two fen nine li six hao thick.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller chimes are thicker in body: the Huangzhong chime is seven fen, two li, and nine hao thick, increasing to the Yingzhong chime at one cun, two fen, nine li, and six hao.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之磬，十一月用之；

translations.literal: The Huangzhong chime is used in the eleventh month;
translations.idiomatic: The Huangzhong chime is used in the eleventh month;

sentences.zh: 大呂之磬，十二月用之；

translations.literal: The Dalü chime is used in the twelfth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Dalü chime is used in the twelfth month;

sentences.zh: 太簇之磬，正月用之；

translations.literal: The Taicu chime is used in the first month;
translations.idiomatic: The Taicu chime is used in the first month;

sentences.zh: 夾鍾之磬，二月用之；

translations.literal: The Jiazhong chime is used in the second month;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiazhong chime is used in the second month;

sentences.zh: 姑洗之磬，三月用之；

translations.literal: The Guxi chime is used in the third month;
translations.idiomatic: The Guxi chime is used in the third month;

sentences.zh: 仲呂之磬，四月用之；

translations.literal: The Zhonglü chime is used in the fourth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhonglü chime is used in the fourth month;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之磬，五月用之；

translations.literal: The Ruibin chime is used in the fifth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Ruibin chime is used in the fifth month;

sentences.zh: 林鍾之磬，六月用之；

translations.literal: The Linzhong chime is used in the sixth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Linzhong chime is used in the sixth month;

sentences.zh: 夷則之磬，七月用之；

translations.literal: The Yize chime is used in the seventh month;
translations.idiomatic: The Yize chime is used in the seventh month;

sentences.zh: 南呂之磬，八月用之；

translations.literal: The Nanlü chime is used in the eighth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Nanlü chime is used in the eighth month;

sentences.zh: 無射之磬，九月用之；

translations.literal: The Wushe chime is used in the ninth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Wushe chime is used in the ninth month;

sentences.zh: 應鍾之磬，十月用之；

translations.literal: The Yingzhong chime is used in the tenth month;
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhong chime is used in the tenth month;

sentences.zh: 磬之簨虡亦四，惟上簨左右刻鳳首，趺飾臥鳧，白羽硃喙。

translations.literal: The chime frames also number four; only the upper crossbars are carved with phoenix heads left and right; the base is decorated with recumbent mandarin ducks, white-feathered with vermilion beaks.
translations.idiomatic: Chime frames likewise number four, but their upper crossbars are carved with phoenix heads at either end, and the base is adorned with recumbent mandarin ducks—white-plumed, vermilion-beaked.

sentences.zh: 十二磬不並陳，當月則懸其一，與鎛鍾同。

translations.literal: The twelve chimes are not displayed together; in the appropriate month only one is suspended, the same as for bo bells.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve chimes are never displayed together; only the chime for the current month is hung, following the same rule as the bo bells.

sentences.zh: 編鐘，範金為之，十六鍾同虡，應十二正律、四倍律，夷則、南呂、無射、應鍾各有倍律。

translations.literal: Serial bells are cast from metal; sixteen bells share one frame, corresponding to the twelve primary pitch pipes and four doubled pitch pipes; Yize, Nanlü, Wushe, and Yingzhong each have a doubled pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Serial bells are cast in metal—sixteen on a single frame, matching the twelve primary pipes and four doubled pipes; Yize, Nanlü, Wushe, and Yingzhong each have a doubled variant.

sentences.zh: 陰陽各八。

translations.literal: Yin and yang, eight each.
translations.idiomatic: Eight for the yin series and eight for the yang.

sentences.zh: 外形橢圓，大小同制，惟內高、內徑、容積各不同。

translations.literal: The outer form is oval; size and construction are uniform, but inner height, inner diameter, and volume each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they are oval and uniform in outer dimensions, but inner height, inner diameter, and volume differ from bell to bell.

sentences.zh: 實體之薄厚，以次遞增。

translations.literal: The thickness of the solid body increases in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The thickness of the bell wall increases step by step.

sentences.zh: 第一倍夷則之鐘，體厚一分三釐三豪，至第十六應鍾之鐘，體厚二分八釐四豪。

translations.literal: The first, doubled Yize bell, body one fen three li three hao thick; to the sixteenth Yingzhong bell, body two fen eight li four hao thick.
translations.idiomatic: The first bell—the doubled Yize—has a wall one fen, three li, and three hao thick; the sixteenth, the Yingzhong, two fen, eight li, and four hao.

sentences.zh: 簨虡塗金，上簨左右刻龍首，中、下二簨俱刻朵雲，系金鉤懸鐘。

translations.literal: The frame is gilded; the upper crossbar is carved with dragon heads left and right; the middle and lower crossbars are both carved with cloud clusters; golden hooks are attached to suspend the bells.
translations.idiomatic: The frame is gilded. Dragon heads adorn either end of the upper crossbar; the middle and lower crossbars bear cloud-cluster carvings, and golden hooks suspend the bells.

sentences.zh: 兩虡承以五采伏獅，下為趺，鏤山水形。

translations.literal: The two frames are supported by five-colored crouching lions; below is the base, engraved in mountain-and-water form.
translations.idiomatic: The two side frames rest on five-colored crouching lions, with a base below engraved in mountain-and-water motifs.

sentences.zh: 編磬，以靈壁石或碧玉為之，十六磬同虡，應十二正律、四倍律，與編鐘同。

translations.literal: Serial chimes are made of Lingbi stone or green jade; sixteen chimes share one frame, corresponding to the twelve primary pitch pipes and four doubled pitch pipes, the same as serial bells.
translations.idiomatic: Serial chimes are fashioned from Lingbi stone or green jade—sixteen on one frame, matching the twelve primary pipes and four doubled pipes, as with the serial bells.

sentences.zh: 陰陽各八。

translations.literal: Yin and yang, eight each.
translations.idiomatic: Eight for the yin series and eight for the yang.

sentences.zh: 皆為鈍角矩形，大小同制。

translations.literal: All are blunt-cornered rectangles, uniform in size and construction.
translations.idiomatic: All are blunt-cornered rectangles of uniform outer dimensions.

sentences.zh: 股長七寸二分九釐，鼓長一尺九分三釐五豪，惟實體之薄厚，以次遞增。

translations.literal: Thigh seven cun two fen nine li in length, drum one chi nine fen three li five hao in length; only the thickness of the solid body increases in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The thigh measures seven cun, two fen, and nine li; the drum one chi, nine fen, three li, and five hao—only the body thickness increases step by step.

sentences.zh: 第一倍夷則之磬，厚六分六豪八絲，至第十六應鍾之磬，厚一寸二分九釐六豪。

translations.literal: The first, doubled Yize chime, six fen six hao eight si thick; to the sixteenth Yingzhong chime, one cun two fen nine li six hao thick.
translations.idiomatic: The first chime—the doubled Yize—is six fen, six hao, and eight si thick; the sixteenth, the Yingzhong, one cun, two fen, nine li, and six hao.

sentences.zh: 簨虡制同編鐘，惟上簨左右刻鳳首，趺飾臥鳧，白羽硃喙。

translations.literal: The frame is constructed the same as for serial bells, except the upper crossbar is carved with phoenix heads left and right; the base is decorated with recumbent mandarin ducks, white-feathered with vermilion beaks.
translations.idiomatic: The frame follows the serial-bell design, except that phoenix heads are carved at either end of the upper crossbar and the base bears recumbent mandarin ducks—white-plumed, vermilion-beaked.

sentences.zh: 建鼓，木匡冒革，貫以柱而樹之。

translations.literal: The set-up drum has a wooden frame covered with hide, pierced by a pillar and set upright.
translations.idiomatic: The set-up drum has a wooden frame covered with hide, mounted upright on a central pillar.

sentences.zh: 面徑二尺三寸四釐，匡長三尺四寸五分七釐，匡半穿方孔，貫柱上出擎蓋，下植至趺。

translations.literal: Face diameter two chi three cun four li; frame length three chi four cun five fen seven li; the frame is half-pierced with a square hole through which the pillar passes, rising above to support the canopy, planted below to the base.
translations.idiomatic: The drumhead measures two chi, three cun, and four li in diameter; the frame is three chi, four cun, five fen, and seven li long. A square hole pierces the frame halfway; the pillar passes through, rising to support a canopy above and set into the base below.

sentences.zh: 蓋上穹下方，頂塗金，上植金鸞為飾。

translations.literal: The canopy is domed above and square below; the top is gilded, with a golden luan bird planted on it as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy is domed on top and square below, gilded at the summit and crowned with a golden luan bird.

sentences.zh: 承鼓以曲木，四歧抱匡，趺四足，各飾臥獅。

translations.literal: The drum is supported by curved wood; four branches embrace the frame; the base has four feet, each decorated with a recumbent lion.
translations.idiomatic: Curved timbers support the drum, four arms clasping the frame; the four-footed base bears a recumbent lion on each foot.

sentences.zh: 擊以雙桴，直柄圓首，凡鼓桴皆如之。

translations.literal: It is struck with paired mallets, straight-handled with round heads; all drum mallets are like this.
translations.idiomatic: It is played with paired mallets—straight shafts, round heads—as are all drumsticks.

sentences.zh: 篪二，皆截竹為質，間纏以絲，橫吹之。

translations.literal: Two chi flutes; both are cut bamboo in substance, wrapped between with silk, blown horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: There are two chi, both cut from bamboo and wrapped with silk at intervals, played horizontally.

sentences.zh: 一孔上出為吹口，五孔外出，一孔內出，又二孔並間下出為出音孔。

translations.literal: One hole opens upward as the blow hole; five holes open outward; one hole opens inward; and two holes open downward side by side between the joints as tone holes.
translations.idiomatic: One hole opens upward as the mouthpiece; five face outward, one inward, and two more open downward between the joints as tone holes.

sentences.zh: 管末有底，中開一孔，吹孔上留竹節以閉音。

translations.literal: The tube end has a bottom; a hole is opened in the center; above the blow hole a bamboo node is left to stop the tone.
translations.idiomatic: The lower end is stopped; a hole is pierced in its center, and a bamboo node is left above the mouthpiece to seal the bore.

sentences.zh: 一姑洗篪，徑八分七釐，自吹口至管末，九寸九分五釐九豪，陽月用之。

translations.literal: One Guxi chi, diameter eight fen seven li, from blow hole to tube end nine cun nine fen five li nine hao, used in yang months.
translations.idiomatic: One Guxi chi, eight fen and seven li in diameter, nine cun, nine fen, five li, and nine hao from mouthpiece to end—used in yang months.

sentences.zh: 一仲呂篪，徑八分三釐二豪，自吹口至管末，九寸五分二釐五豪，陰月用之。

translations.literal: One Zhonglü chi, diameter eight fen three li two hao, from blow hole to tube end nine cun five fen two li five hao, used in yin months.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhonglü chi, eight fen, three li, and two hao in diameter, nine cun, five fen, two li, and five hao from mouthpiece to end—used in yin months.

sentences.zh: 排簫，比竹為之，其形參差象鳳翼。

translations.literal: Panpipes are made of bundled bamboo; their form is staggered, resembling phoenix wings.
translations.idiomatic: Panpipes are assembled from matched bamboo tubes, their staggered lengths shaped like phoenix wings.

sentences.zh: 十六管，陰陽各八，同徑殊長。

translations.literal: Sixteen tubes; yin and yang eight each; same diameter, different lengths.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen tubes—eight yin and eight yang—of uniform bore but varying length.

sentences.zh: 上開山口單吹之，無旁出孔。

translations.literal: The upper end is opened at the mountain mouth and blown singly; there are no side holes.
translations.idiomatic: Each tube is blown at its open upper end; there are no lateral holes.

sentences.zh: 自左而右，列二倍律、夷則，無射。

translations.literal: From left to right are arranged two doubled pitch pipes, Yize, and Wushe.
translations.idiomatic: From left to right stand two doubled pipes, then Yize and Wushe.

sentences.zh: 六正律以協陽均。

translations.literal: Six primary pitch pipes to harmonize the yang scale.
translations.idiomatic: Six primary pipes harmonize the yang scale.

sentences.zh: 自右而左，列二倍呂，南呂，應鍾。

translations.literal: From right to left are arranged two doubled pitch pipes, Nanlü, and Yingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From right to left stand two doubled pipes, then Nanlü and Yingzhong.

sentences.zh: 六正呂以協陰均。

translations.literal: Six primary pitch pipes to harmonize the yin scale.
translations.idiomatic: Six primary pipes harmonize the yin scale.

sentences.zh: 管面各鐫律呂名，納於一櫝，而齊其吹口。

translations.literal: Each tube face is engraved with the pitch-pipe name; they are fitted into one case, with their blow holes aligned.
translations.idiomatic: Each tube is engraved with its pitch name, fitted into a single case with the mouthpieces aligned.

sentences.zh: 櫝用木，形如幾，虛其中以受管。

translations.literal: The case is of wood, shaped like a low table, hollow within to receive the tubes.
translations.idiomatic: The case is wooden, table-shaped, hollow inside to hold the tubes.

sentences.zh: 塤有二，燒土為之，形皆橢圓如鵝子，上銳下平。

translations.literal: Two xun ocarinas; both are fired clay, oval in form like goose eggs, pointed above and flat below.
translations.idiomatic: There are two xun, both of fired clay, oval as goose eggs—pointed above, flat below.

sentences.zh: 前四孔，後二孔，頂上一孔，以手捧而吹之。

translations.literal: Four holes in front, two behind, one on top; it is blown cupped in the hands.
translations.idiomatic: Four holes face forward, two aft, one on top; the player cups it in both hands to blow.

sentences.zh: 一黃鍾塤，內高二寸二分三釐，腹徑一寸七分一釐七豪，底徑一寸一分六釐八豪，陽月用之。

translations.literal: One Huangzhong xun, inner height two cun two fen three li, belly diameter one cun seven fen one li seven hao, base diameter one cun one fen six li eight hao, used in yang months.
translations.idiomatic: One Huangzhong xun, two cun, two fen, and three li high inside, one cun, seven fen, one li, and seven hao across the belly, one cun, one fen, six li, and eight hao at the base—used in yang months.

sentences.zh: 一大呂塤，內高二寸一分三釐三豪，腹徑一寸六分四釐二豪，底徑一寸一分一釐七豪，陰月用之。

translations.literal: One Dalü xun, inner height two cun one fen three li three hao, belly diameter one cun six fen four li two hao, base diameter one cun one fen one li seven hao, used in yin months.
translations.idiomatic: One Dalü xun, two cun, one fen, three li, and three hao high inside, one cun, six fen, four li, and two hao across the belly, one cun, one fen, one li, and seven hao at the base—used in yin months.

sentences.zh: 簫二，截竹為之，皆上開山口，五孔前出，一孔後出，出音孔二，相對旁出。

translations.literal: Two xiao flutes; cut bamboo; all open at the mountain mouth above; five holes open forward, one backward; two tone holes open sideways opposite each other.
translations.idiomatic: There are two xiao, cut from bamboo, each open at the upper end; five holes face forward, one aft, and two tone holes open on opposite sides.

sentences.zh: 一姑洗簫，徑四分三釐五豪，自山口至出音孔，長一尺五寸八分四釐二豪，陽月用之。

translations.literal: One Guxi xiao, diameter four fen three li five hao, from mountain mouth to tone hole one chi five cun eight fen four li two hao in length, used in yang months.
translations.idiomatic: One Guxi xiao, four fen, three li, and five hao in diameter, one chi, five cun, eight fen, four li, and two hao from upper end to tone hole—used in yang months.

sentences.zh: 一仲呂簫，徑四分一釐六豪，自山口至出音孔，長一尺五寸一分五釐二豪，陰月用之。

translations.literal: One Zhonglü xiao, diameter four fen one li six hao, from mountain mouth to tone hole one chi five cun one fen five li two hao in length, used in yin months.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhonglü xiao, four fen, one li, and six hao in diameter, one chi, five cun, one fen, five li, and two hao from upper end to tone hole—used in yin months.

sentences.zh: 笛二，截竹為之，皆間纏以絲，兩端加龍首龍尾。

translations.literal: Two di flutes; cut bamboo; all wrapped between with silk; dragon head and dragon tail added at both ends.
translations.idiomatic: There are two di, cut from bamboo and wrapped with silk at intervals, with dragon-head and dragon-tail fittings at either end.

sentences.zh: 左一孔，另吹孔，次孔加竹膜，右六孔，皆上出。

translations.literal: One hole on the left, a separate blow hole; the next hole fitted with a bamboo membrane; six holes on the right, all opening upward.
translations.idiomatic: One hole on the left, then a separate mouth hole with a bamboo membrane over the next; six holes on the right, all opening upward.

sentences.zh: 出音孔二，相對旁出。

translations.literal: Two tone holes, opening sideways opposite each other.
translations.idiomatic: Two tone holes open on opposite sides.

sentences.zh: 末二孔，亦上出。

translations.literal: The last two holes also open upward.
translations.idiomatic: The final two holes also open upward.

sentences.zh: 一姑洗笛，徑四分三釐五豪，自吹孔右盡，通長一尺二寸五分一釐七豪，陽月用之。

translations.literal: One Guxi di, diameter four fen three li five hao, from the blow hole to the right end, total length one chi two cun five fen one li seven hao, used in yang months.
translations.idiomatic: One Guxi di, four fen, three li, and five hao in diameter, one chi, two cun, five fen, one li, and seven hao from mouth hole to far end—used in yang months.

sentences.zh: 一仲呂笛，徑四分一釐六豪，自吹孔右盡，通長一尺一寸九分七釐二豪，陰月用之。

translations.literal: One Zhonglü di, diameter four fen one li six hao, from the blow hole to the right end, total length one chi one cun nine fen seven li two hao, used in yin months.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhonglü di, four fen, one li, and six hao in diameter, one chi, one cun, nine fen, seven li, and two hao from mouth hole to far end—used in yin months.

sentences.zh: 琴，面用桐，底用梓，魨以漆。

translations.literal: The qin: the face uses paulownia, the base uses catalpa, coated with lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: The qin has a paulownia soundboard, a catalpa back, and a lacquered finish.

sentences.zh: 前廣、後狹、上圓、下方、中虛。

translations.literal: Wide in front, narrow in back, round above, square below, hollow within.
translations.idiomatic: It is broad at the front and narrow at the rear, round on top and square below, with a hollow interior.

sentences.zh: 通長三尺一寸五分九釐。

translations.literal: Total length three chi one cun five fen nine li.
translations.idiomatic: Its overall length is three chi, one cun, five fen, and nine li.

sentences.zh: 底孔二，上曰龍池，下曰鳳池。

translations.literal: Two holes in the base; the upper is called the Dragon Pool, the lower the Phoenix Pool.
translations.idiomatic: There are two sound holes in the base—the upper called the Dragon Pool, the lower the Phoenix Pool.

sentences.zh: 腹內有天地二柱，天柱圓，當肩下；

translations.literal: Within the belly are two pillars, Heaven and Earth; the Heaven pillar is round, placed below the shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: Inside the body are two sound posts—the Heaven post, round, set below the shoulders;

sentences.zh: 地柱方，當腰上。

translations.literal: The Earth pillar is square, placed above the waist.
translations.idiomatic: and the Earth post, square, set above the waist.

sentences.zh: 凡七弦，皆硃。

translations.literal: Seven strings in all, all vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: All seven strings are vermilion.

sentences.zh: 第一弦一百八綸，第二弦九十六綸，第三弦八十一綸，第四弦七十二綸，第五弦六十四綸，第六弦五十四綸，第七弦四十八綸。

translations.literal: The first string one hundred eight strands, the second ninety-six strands, the third eighty-one strands, the fourth seventy-two strands, the fifth sixty-four strands, the sixth fifty-four strands, the seventh forty-eight strands.
translations.idiomatic: The first string has one hundred eight strands, the second ninety-six, the third eighty-one, the fourth seventy-two, the fifth sixty-four, the sixth fifty-four, and the seventh forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 軫七，徽十三。

translations.literal: Seven tuning pegs, thirteen harmonic markers.
translations.idiomatic: There are seven tuning pegs and thirteen harmonic markers.

sentences.zh: 其飾岳山焦尾用紫檀，徽用螺蚌，軫結黃絨紃，承以魨漆幾。

translations.literal: Its ornamentation: the bridge and scorched tail use red sandalwood; the harmonic markers use mother-of-pearl; the pegs are tied with yellow velvet cords; it rests on a lacquered stand.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge and scorched tail are of red sandalwood, the harmonic markers of mother-of-pearl; the pegs are strung with yellow velvet cords, and the instrument rests on a lacquered stand.

sentences.zh: 瑟體用桐，魨以漆，前廣、後狹、面圓、底平、中高、兩端俯。

translations.literal: The se body uses paulownia, coated with lacquer; wide in front, narrow in back, round-faced, flat-bottomed, high in the middle, both ends sloping downward.
translations.idiomatic: The se body is paulownia, lacquered—broad at the front, narrow at the rear, with a rounded face, flat base, a raised center, and both ends sloping down.

sentences.zh: 通長六尺五寸六分一釐。

translations.literal: Total length six chi five cun six fen one li.
translations.idiomatic: Its overall length is six chi, five cun, six fen, and one li.

sentences.zh: 底孔二，是為越。

translations.literal: Two holes in the base—these are called the sound openings.
translations.idiomatic: Two holes pierce the base—these are the sound openings.

sentences.zh: 前越四齣，後越上圓下平。

translations.literal: The front opening has four notches; the rear opening is round above and flat below.
translations.idiomatic: The front opening has four notches; the rear is round on top and flat below.

sentences.zh: 凡二十五弦，弦皆二百四十三綸。

translations.literal: Twenty-five strings in all; each string has two hundred forty-three strands.
translations.idiomatic: There are twenty-five strings, each of two hundred forty-three strands.

sentences.zh: 中一弦黃，兩旁皆硃。

translations.literal: The center string is yellow; those on either side are all vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: The center string is yellow; those on either side are vermilion.

sentences.zh: 設柱和弦，柱無定位，各隨宮調。

translations.literal: Movable bridges are set to tune the strings; the bridges have no fixed position, each following the mode.
translations.idiomatic: Movable bridges tune the strings; they have no fixed placement but shift with each mode.

sentences.zh: 弦孔飾螺蚌，承以魨金幾二。

translations.literal: The string holes are ornamented with mother-of-pearl; it rests on two lacquered gilded stands.
translations.idiomatic: The string holes are inlaid with mother-of-pearl, and the instrument rests on two lacquered, gilded stands.

sentences.zh: 笙二，截紫竹為管，環植匏中，匏或以木代之。

translations.literal: Two sheng; purple bamboo is cut for pipes and planted in a ring within the gourd; the gourd may be replaced with wood.
translations.idiomatic: There are two sheng: pipes cut from purple bamboo set in a ring within a gourd body, which may be replaced by wood.

sentences.zh: 管皆十七，束以竹，本豐末斂，管本近底削半露竅。

translations.literal: All pipes number seventeen; bound with bamboo; thick at the base, tapering at the tip; near the base each pipe is half-cut to expose the opening.
translations.idiomatic: Each has seventeen pipes, bound with bamboo—thick at the base, tapering toward the tips; near the base each pipe is half-cut to expose its opening.

sentences.zh: 以薄銅葉為簧，點以蠟珠，其上各按律呂分開出音孔。

translations.literal: Thin copper leaves serve as reeds, dotted with wax beads; above them tone holes are opened according to each pitch pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Thin copper reeds, tipped with wax beads, sit beneath tone holes opened according to the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 匏之半施橢圓短嘴，昂其末。

translations.literal: On half the gourd an oval short mouthpiece is fitted, its end raised upward.
translations.idiomatic: Half the gourd bears an oval short mouthpiece with its tip raised.

sentences.zh: 中為方孔，別為長嘴如鳳頸，置於短嘴方孔中。

translations.literal: In the center is a square hole; a separate long mouthpiece like a phoenix neck is placed in the square hole of the short mouthpiece.
translations.idiomatic: A square hole pierces its center; a separate long mouthpiece shaped like a phoenix neck fits into that square opening.

sentences.zh: 末為吹口，氣從吹口入，鼓簧成音。

translations.literal: The end is the blow hole; breath enters through the blow hole and vibrates the reeds to produce sound.
translations.idiomatic: Its tip is the mouth hole; breath enters there and sets the reeds vibrating to produce tone.

sentences.zh: 小笙制如大笙而小，亦十七管，惟第一、第九、第十六、第十七管不設簧，有簧者凡十三管，餘均與大笙同。

translations.literal: The small sheng is constructed like the large sheng but smaller; also seventeen pipes; only the first, ninth, sixteenth, and seventeenth pipes have no reeds—those with reeds number thirteen pipes in all; the rest is the same as the large sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The small sheng follows the large sheng's design but smaller, likewise with seventeen pipes—though the first, ninth, sixteenth, and seventeenth lack reeds, leaving thirteen reeded pipes; all else matches the large sheng.

sentences.zh: 搏拊，如鼓而小。

translations.literal: Hand clappers, like a drum but small.
translations.idiomatic: Hand clappers resemble small drums.

sentences.zh: 面徑七寸二分九釐，匡長一尺四寸五分八釐。

translations.literal: Face diameter seven cun two fen nine li; frame length one chi four cun five fen eight li.
translations.idiomatic: The head measures seven cun, two fen, and nine li in diameter; the frame is one chi, four cun, five fen, and eight li long.

sentences.zh: 匡上施金盤龍二，銜小金鐶，以黃絨紃系之，橫置趺上。

translations.literal: On the frame are set two gilded coiled dragons, each holding a small golden ring, tied with yellow velvet cords, placed horizontally on the base.
translations.idiomatic: Two gilded coiled dragons on the frame hold small golden rings tied with yellow velvet cords; the clappers lie horizontally on the base.

sentences.zh: 用時懸於項，擊以左右手。

translations.literal: When in use they are hung at the neck and struck with both hands.
translations.idiomatic: In performance they hang from the neck and are struck with both hands.

sentences.zh: 每建鼓一擊，則搏拊兩擊以為節。

translations.literal: For each one stroke of the set-up drum, the hand clappers strike twice as beat.
translations.idiomatic: For every stroke of the set-up drum, the hand clappers strike twice to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: 柷，以木為之，形如方斗，上廣下狹，三面正中各隆起為圓形以受擊，一面中為圓孔以出音。

translations.literal: The zhù is made of wood, shaped like a square bucket, wide above and narrow below; on three faces the center each rises in a round form to receive strikes; on one face the center is a round hole for sound emission.
translations.idiomatic: The zhù is wooden, bucket-shaped—wide above, narrow below. Three faces bear a raised round striking surface at center; the fourth has a round sound hole at center.

sentences.zh: 以趺承之，擊具曰止。

translations.literal: It is supported on a base; the striker is called zhi.
translations.idiomatic: It rests on a base; its striker is called the zhi.

sentences.zh: 敔，以木為之，形如伏虎，背上有二十七齟齬刻，以趺承之。

translations.literal: The yù is made of wood, shaped like a crouching tiger; on its back are twenty-seven serrated ridges; it is supported on a base.
translations.idiomatic: The yù is wooden, shaped like a crouching tiger with twenty-seven serrated ridges along its back, resting on a base.

sentences.zh: 鼓之以籈，以竹為之，析其半為二十四莖，於齟齬上橫轢之。

translations.literal: It is scraped with a zhēn; made of bamboo, split in half into twenty-four stalks, scraped horizontally across the serrated ridges.
translations.idiomatic: It is scraped with a zhēn—a bamboo rod split into twenty-four stalks and drawn horizontally across the ridges.

sentences.zh: 麾，黃帛為之，綉九曲雲龍。

translations.literal: The baton is made of yellow silk, embroidered with nine-fold cloud-and-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The conductor's baton is yellow silk embroidered with nine-fold cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 上飾藍帛，綉紅日，日中綉中和字。

translations.literal: Above is ornamented with blue silk, embroidered with a red sun; within the sun is embroidered the character for Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Blue silk adorns the upper portion, embroidered with a red sun bearing the character Zhonghe at its center.

sentences.zh: 上綉三台星，左北斗，右南斗。

translations.literal: Above are embroidered the Three Steps stars; to the left the Northern Dipper, to the right the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Above are embroidered the Three Steps; the Northern Dipper to the left, the Southern Dipper to the right.

sentences.zh: 帛上下施橫木，上鏤雙龍，下為山水形，皆魨金。

translations.literal: Horizontal timbers are fitted above and below the silk; the upper is carved with paired dragons, the lower in mountain-and-water form; all are lacquered and gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Horizontal timbers frame the silk above and below—the upper carved with paired dragons, the lower with mountains and waters—all lacquered and gilded.

sentences.zh: 硃杠，上曲為龍首以懸麾，麾舉樂作，麾偃樂止。

translations.literal: A vermilion pole, curved at the top into a dragon head to suspend the baton; when the baton is raised, music begins; when lowered, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion pole curves at the top into a dragon head from which the baton hangs—raise it and music begins; lower it and music stops.

sentences.zh: 丹陛大樂，凡御殿受賀及宮中行禮皆用之。

translations.literal: Danbi Grand Music is used whenever the emperor receives felicitations in the hall and whenever ceremonies are performed within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Danbi Grand Music accompanies imperial audiences receiving felicitations and all ceremonial rites within the palace.

sentences.zh: 其器：戲竹二，大鼓二，方響二，雲鑼二，簫二，管四，笛四，笙四，杖鼓一，拍板一。

translations.literal: Its instruments: two conductor's bamboo clappers, two large drums, two square chime sets, two cloud gongs, two xiao, four guan pipes, four di, four sheng, one stick drum, one clapper board.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments are two conductor's bamboo clappers, two large drums, two square chime sets, two cloud gongs, two xiao, four guan pipes, four di, four sheng, one stick drum, and one clapper board.

sentences.zh: 簫、笛、笙同中和韶樂。

translations.literal: Xiao, di, and sheng are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music.
translations.idiomatic: The xiao, di, and sheng match those of Zhonghe Shao Music.

sentences.zh: 戲竹，析竹為之，凡二，各五十莖。

translations.literal: Conductor's bamboo clappers are split from bamboo; two in all, fifty stalks each.
translations.idiomatic: Conductor's bamboo clappers are split bamboo—two sets of fifty stalks each.

sentences.zh: 魨硃，承以塗金壺盧，下有柄，亦魨硃。

translations.literal: Lacquered vermilion; supported on a gilded gourd-shaped holder; below is a handle, also lacquered vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: They are lacquered vermilion, mounted on gilded gourd-shaped holders with vermilion-lacquered handles below.

sentences.zh: 人各執其一，立丹陛上，合則樂作，分則樂止。

translations.literal: Each person holds one, standing on the cinnabar steps; when joined together music begins, when separated music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Each performer holds one set, standing on the cinnabar steps—bring them together and music begins; separate them and music stops.

sentences.zh: 戲音與麾同，其用亦與麾同。

translations.literal: The clapper signal is the same as the baton; its use is also the same as the baton.
translations.idiomatic: The clapper signal matches the baton, and its function is the same.

sentences.zh: 大鼓，木匡冒革，面徑三尺六寸四分五釐，匡高三尺二寸四分。

translations.literal: Large drums have wooden frames covered with hide; face diameter three chi six cun four fen five li; frame height three chi two cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Large drums have wooden frames covered with hide—the head three chi, six cun, four fen, and five li in diameter, the frame three chi, two cun, and four fen high.

sentences.zh: 腹施銅膽，面魨黃，繪五采雲龍。

translations.literal: A copper resonator is fitted in the belly; the face is lacquered yellow, painted with five-colored cloud-and-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: A copper resonator fills the belly; the head is lacquered yellow and painted with five-colored cloud-and-dragon designs.

sentences.zh: 匡魨硃，繪交龍，匡半金鐶四。

translations.literal: The frame is lacquered vermilion, painted with interlaced dragons; four golden rings at mid-frame.
translations.idiomatic: The frame is lacquered vermilion with interlaced dragons painted upon it; four golden rings ring the frame at mid-height.

sentences.zh: 承以魨硃架，架有鉤，以鉤鐶平懸之。

translations.literal: Supported on a lacquered vermilion stand; the stand has hooks; hung level by hooking the rings.
translations.idiomatic: It rests on a lacquered vermilion stand fitted with hooks that suspend the drum level by its rings.

sentences.zh: 架高六尺，鼓者藉蹈以擊之。

translations.literal: The stand is six chi high; the drummer steps on it to strike.
translations.idiomatic: The stand stands six chi high; the drummer steps upon it to play.

sentences.zh: 方響，以鋼為之，形長方，十六枚同虡，應十二正律、四倍律，與編鐘、磬同。

translations.literal: Square chimes are made of steel, rectangular in form; sixteen pieces share one frame, corresponding to the twelve primary pitch pipes and four doubled pitch pipes, the same as serial bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Square chimes are steel rectangles—sixteen on one frame, matching the twelve primary pipes and four doubled pipes, as with serial bells and chimes.

sentences.zh: 形質皆同。

translations.literal: Form and substance are all the same.
translations.idiomatic: All share the same form and material.

sentences.zh: 惟以薄厚為次。

translations.literal: Only thickness serves as the gradation.
translations.idiomatic: Only thickness varies among them.

sentences.zh: 倍夷則之厚，三分三豪四絲，遞增至應鍾之厚，六分四釐八豪。

translations.literal: The doubled Yize thickness three fen three hao four si; increasing in succession to the Yingzhong thickness six fen four li eight hao.
translations.idiomatic: The doubled Yize piece is three fen, three hao, and four si thick, increasing step by step to the Yingzhong at six fen, four li, and eight hao.

sentences.zh: 後面近上三分之一皆為橫脊，竅其上端，系以黃絨紃，懸於虡而斜倚之，擊以小鋼槌。

translations.literal: On the rear face near the upper third all form a horizontal ridge; a hole is pierced at its upper end; tied with yellow velvet cords; suspended on the frame and leaned at an angle; struck with a small steel mallet.
translations.idiomatic: The upper third of the rear face forms a horizontal ridge with a hole at its top; yellow velvet cords suspend each piece on the frame at an angle, and it is struck with a small steel mallet.

sentences.zh: 各部樂皆同，惟馬上凱歌樂分用其八，人各一枚，擎而擊之。

translations.literal: All music sections are the same; only mounted victory-song music uses eight of them separately, each person one piece, held aloft and struck.
translations.idiomatic: All music sections use the same design; only mounted victory-song music divides eight pieces among the players, each holding one aloft to strike.

sentences.zh: 雲鑼，范銅為之，十枚同架，應四正律、六半律，姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射四正律，半黃鍾至半無射六半律。

translations.literal: Cloud gongs are cast from copper; ten pieces share one frame, corresponding to four primary pitch pipes and six half-pitch pipes: Guxi, Ruibin, Yize, and Wushe as the four primary pipes; half Huangzhong through half Wushe as the six half-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud gongs are cast copper—ten on one frame, matching four primary pipes and six half-pipes: Guxi, Ruibin, Yize, and Wushe among the primaries, and half Huangzhong through half Wushe among the halves.

sentences.zh: 皆四旁穿竅，以黃絨紃繫於架，中四，左右各三，合三行為九宮形，其一上出。

translations.literal: All are pierced with holes on four sides; tied with yellow velvet cords to the frame; four in the center, three each left and right; together three rows form a nine-palace shape, one projecting upward.
translations.idiomatic: Each is pierced on four sides and tied to the frame with yellow velvet cords—four at center, three on each flank—arranged in three rows forming a nine-palace pattern with one gong projecting above.

sentences.zh: 以薄厚為次，下右應姑洗之律，厚二釐五豪二絲。

translations.literal: Thickness serves as the gradation; lower right corresponds to the Guxi pitch pipe, thickness two li five hao two si.
translations.idiomatic: Thickness marks the gradation—the lower right gong matches the Guxi pipe at two li, five hao, and two si thick.

sentences.zh: 遞增至最上，應半無射之律，厚五釐九豪八絲。

translations.literal: Increasing in succession to the topmost, corresponding to the half Wushe pitch pipe, thickness five li nine hao eight si.
translations.idiomatic: Thickness increases step by step to the topmost gong, matching half Wushe at five li, nine hao, and eight si.

sentences.zh: 管即頭管，以堅木或骨角為之，大小各一，皆前七孔後一孔，管端設蘆哨，入管吹之。

translations.literal: Guan pipes are lead pipes, made of hard wood or bone and horn; one large and one small; all have seven holes in front and one behind; a reed mouthpiece is set at the pipe end; blown into the pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Guan pipes—lead pipes of hard wood or bone and horn, one large and one small—each have seven front holes and one back hole, with a reed mouthpiece at the tip through which the player blows.

sentences.zh: 大管以姑洗律管為體，徑二分七釐四豪，哨下口至末，長五寸七分六釐。

translations.literal: The large pipe uses the Guxi pitch pipe as its body; diameter two fen seven li four hao; from below the mouthpiece to the end, length five cun seven fen six li.
translations.idiomatic: The large pipe follows the Guxi pitch pipe in bore—two fen, seven li, and four hao in diameter, five cun, seven fen, and six li from below the mouthpiece to the end.

sentences.zh: 小管以黃鍾半積同形管為體，徑二分一釐七豪，哨下口至末，長五寸六分二豪。

translations.literal: The small pipe uses the half Huangzhong pipe of equal volume and same form as its body; diameter two fen one li seven hao; from below the mouthpiece to the end, length five cun six fen two hao.
translations.idiomatic: The small pipe follows the half Huangzhong pipe in bore—two fen, one li, and seven hao in diameter, five cun, six fen, and two hao from below the mouthpiece to the end.

sentences.zh: 皆間束以絲，兩端以象牙為飾。

translations.literal: All are wrapped between with silk; both ends ornamented with ivory.
translations.idiomatic: Both are wrapped with silk at intervals, with ivory fittings at either end.

sentences.zh: 杖鼓，上下二面，鐵圈冒革，復楦以木匡，細腰。

translations.literal: Stick drums have upper and lower faces; iron rings covered with hide, further mounted on a wooden frame, with a narrow waist.
translations.idiomatic: Stick drums are double-headed—iron rings covered with hide, mounted on a wooden frame with a narrow waist.

sentences.zh: 匡高一尺九寸四分四釐、腰徑二寸八分八釐，兩端徑各八寸一分，上下面徑各一尺二寸九分六釐。

translations.literal: Frame height one chi nine cun four fen four li; waist diameter two cun eight fen eight li; both end diameters eight cun one fen each; upper and lower face diameters one chi two cun nine fen six li each.
translations.idiomatic: The frame stands one chi, nine cun, four fen, and four li high; the waist measures two cun, eight fen, and eight li across; each end eight cun and one fen; each head one chi, two cun, nine fen, and six li in diameter.

sentences.zh: 面匡俱魨黃，繪五采雲龍，緣以綠皮掩錢。

translations.literal: Both face and frame are lacquered yellow, painted with five-colored cloud-and-dragon patterns; edged with green leather studded with coins.
translations.idiomatic: Head and frame are lacquered yellow with five-colored cloud-and-dragon designs, edged in green leather studded with coin-shaped bosses.

sentences.zh: 上下邊綴金鉤各六，以黃絨紃交絡之。

translations.literal: Six golden hooks are attached along each upper and lower edge; tied together with interlaced yellow velvet cords.
translations.idiomatic: Six golden hooks ring each head, laced together with crisscrossed yellow velvet cords.

sentences.zh: 腰加束焉。

translations.literal: The waist is additionally bound.
translations.idiomatic: The waist is further bound with cords.

sentences.zh: 腰飾綠皮焦葉文。

translations.literal: The waist is ornamented with green leather in scorched-leaf patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The waist bears green leather in scorched-leaf patterns.

sentences.zh: 以魨硃竹片擊之。

translations.literal: Struck with lacquered vermilion bamboo slats.
translations.idiomatic: It is played with lacquered vermilion bamboo slats.

sentences.zh: 拍板，以堅木為之，左右各三片。

translations.literal: Clapper boards are made of hard wood; three slats each on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Clapper boards are hard wood—three slats on each side.

sentences.zh: 近上橫穿二孔，以黃絨紃聯之，合擊以為節。

translations.literal: Near the top two holes are pierced horizontally; linked with yellow velvet cords; struck together as beat.
translations.idiomatic: Two holes pierce each slat near the top, linked with yellow velvet cords; the slats are clapped together to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: 中和清樂，用於冊尊典禮，宴饗進饌，除夕、元夕張燈亦用之。

translations.literal: Zhonghe Qing Music is used for investiture and ennoblement ceremonies, banquets when dishes are served, and also on New Year's Eve and the Lantern Festival when lanterns are hung.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe Qing Music accompanies investiture rites, banquets when courses are served, and also New Year's Eve and the Lantern Festival when lanterns are displayed.

sentences.zh: 其器：雲鑼二，笛二，管二，笙二，杖鼓一，手鼓一，拍板一。

translations.literal: Its instruments: two cloud gongs, two di, two guan pipes, two sheng, one stick drum, one hand drum, one clapper board.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments are two cloud gongs, two di, two guan pipes, two sheng, one stick drum, one hand drum, and one clapper board.

sentences.zh: 笛、笙同中和韶樂，雲鑼、管、板同丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Di and sheng are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music; cloud gongs, guan pipes, and clapper boards are the same as in Danbi Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: The di and sheng match Zhonghe Shao Music; the cloud gongs, guan pipes, and clapper boards match Danbi Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 杖鼓同丹陛大樂而小，或半之，或為三之二。

translations.literal: Stick drums are the same as in Danbi Grand Music but smaller, either half the size or two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Stick drums follow the Danbi Grand Music design but smaller—either half size or two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 手鼓，木匡冒革，面徑九寸一分二豪，腰徑一尺二分四釐。

translations.literal: Hand drums have wooden frames covered with hide; face diameter nine cun one fen two hao; waist diameter one chi two fen four li.
translations.idiomatic: Hand drums have wooden frames covered with hide—the head nine cun, one fen, and two hao in diameter, the waist one chi, two fen, and four li across.

sentences.zh: 以柄貫匡，持而擊之。

translations.literal: A handle pierces the frame; held and struck.
translations.idiomatic: A handle passes through the frame; the player holds it and strikes.

sentences.zh: 丹陛清樂，用於宴饗進茶、進酒，臨雍賜茶亦用之。

translations.literal: Danbi Qing Music is used when tea and wine are served at banquets; also used when tea is bestowed at the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Danbi Qing Music accompanies banquets when tea and wine are served, and also when tea is bestowed at the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂器均與中和清樂同。

translations.literal: The instruments are all the same as in Zhonghe Qing Music.
translations.idiomatic: The instruments are identical to those of Zhonghe Qing Music.

sentences.zh: 導迎樂、鐃歌樂，用於乘輿出入。

translations.literal: Processional Welcome Music and Nao Song Music are used when the imperial carriage enters and exits.
translations.idiomatic: Processional Welcome Music and Nao Song Music accompany the imperial carriage on its comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕鹵簿則奏導迎樂，騎駕鹵簿則奏鐃歌之行幸樂，法駕鹵簿、大駕鹵簿則導迎樂間以鐃歌樂，惟大祀詣壇、廟則導迎樂、鐃歌樂設而不作。

translations.literal: For the Luanjia guard array, Processional Welcome Music is performed; for the Qijia guard array, the Nao Song travel music is performed; for the Fajia and Dajia guard arrays, Processional Welcome Music is interspersed with Nao Song Music; only for great sacrifices proceeding to altars and temples are Processional Welcome Music and Nao Song Music set out but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Luanjia guard array plays Processional Welcome Music; the Qijia array plays nao song travel music; the Fajia and Dajia arrays alternate processional welcome music with nao song music—only when proceeding to altars and temples for great sacrifices are both ensembles present but silent.

sentences.zh: 凡三大節進表及進實錄、聖訓、玉牒，又親耕、親蠶、授時、頒詔、殿試、送榜、迎吻，凡前導以御仗出入者，皆奏導迎樂。

translations.literal: Whenever memorials are presented at the three great festivals, and whenever Veritable Records, Sacred Instructions, and Jade Registers are presented; also for the emperor's personal plowing and sericulture, the granting of the calendar, promulgation of edicts, palace examinations, delivery of the examination lists, and welcoming the roof-beam—whenever imperial regalia leads the way in and out, Processional Welcome Music is performed.
translations.idiomatic: Processional Welcome Music accompanies every occasion when imperial regalia leads the way—presentations at the three great festivals, delivery of Veritable Records, Sacred Instructions, and Jade Registers, the emperor's personal plowing and sericulture, calendar distribution, edict promulgation, palace examinations, delivery of the examination lists, and the roof-beam ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌之樂有鹵簿樂，其部一，曰鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: Nao Song music includes guard-array music; one section, called Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music.
translations.idiomatic: Nao song music includes guard-array music—one section called nao song drum-and-pipe music.

sentences.zh: 有前部樂，其部一，曰前部大樂。

translations.literal: There is vanguard music; one section, called Vanguard Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: There is vanguard music—one section called Vanguard Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 亦曰大罕波。

translations.literal: Also called Dahanbo.
translations.idiomatic: It is also called Dahanbo.

sentences.zh: 有行幸樂，其部三：曰鳴角，曰鐃歌大樂，曰鐃歌清樂。

translations.literal: There is travel music; three sections: called Horn Blasts, Nao Song Grand Music, and Nao Song Qing Music.
translations.idiomatic: There is travel music in three sections: Horn Blasts, Nao Song Grand Music, and Nao Song Qing Music.

sentences.zh: 有凱旋樂，其部二：曰鐃歌，曰凱歌。

translations.literal: There is triumphal music; two sections: called Nao Song and Victory Song.
translations.idiomatic: There is triumphal music in two sections: Nao Song and Victory Song.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿樂與前部大樂並列，亦曰金鼓鐃歌大樂，凡圜丘、祈穀、常雩，用大駕鹵簿，則前部大樂、鐃歌鼓吹、行幸樂三部並陳。

translations.literal: Guard-array music and Vanguard Grand Music stand side by side, also called Metal-Drum Nao Song Grand Music; for the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and Regular Supplication for Rain, when the Dajia guard array is used, the three sections—Vanguard Grand Music, Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music, and Travel Music—are all deployed together.
translations.idiomatic: Guard-array music and Vanguard Grand Music stand together, also known as Metal-Drum Nao Song Grand Music. For the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, and Regular Supplication for Rain, when the Dajia guard array is used, all three sections—Vanguard Grand Music, nao song drum-and-pipe music, and travel music—are deployed.

sentences.zh: 方澤，用法駕鹵簿，則陳前部大樂、鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the Square Mound, when the Fajia guard array is used, Vanguard Grand Music and Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music are deployed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Square Mound with the Fajia guard array, Vanguard Grand Music and nao song drum-and-pipe music are deployed.

sentences.zh: 太廟、社稷及各中祀，用法駕鹵簿，則陳鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Altars of Soil and Grain, and various secondary sacrifices, when the Fajia guard array is used, Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music is deployed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Altars of Soil and Grain, and other secondary sacrifices with the Fajia guard array, nao song drum-and-pipe music is deployed.

sentences.zh: 朝會用法駕鹵簿同。

translations.literal: Court assemblies using the Fajia guard array follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Court assemblies with the Fajia guard array follow the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 御樓受俘，用法駕鹵簿，則陳金鼓鐃歌大樂。

translations.literal: When captives are received at the Imperial Tower, with the Fajia guard array, Metal-Drum Nao Song Grand Music is deployed.
translations.idiomatic: When captives are received at the Imperial Tower with the Fajia guard array, Metal-Drum Nao Song Grand Music is deployed.

sentences.zh: 巡幸及大閱，用騎駕鹵簿，則陳鳴角鐃歌大樂、鐃歌清樂。

translations.literal: For imperial tours and grand military reviews, when the Qijia guard array is used, Horn Blasts Nao Song Grand Music and Nao Song Qing Music are deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tours and grand military reviews with the Qijia guard array deploy Horn Blasts Nao Song Grand Music and Nao Song Qing Music.

sentences.zh: 凱旋郊勞，則奏鐃歌。

translations.literal: For triumphal suburban feasts of reward, Nao Song is performed.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban feasts welcoming a victorious return, nao song is performed.

sentences.zh: 迴鑾振旅，則奏凱歌。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returns and the army is reassembled, Victory Song is performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returns and the troops are reassembled, victory song is performed.

sentences.zh: 導迎樂用戲竹二，管六，笛四，笙二，雲鑼二，導迎鼓一，拍板一。

translations.literal: Processional Welcome Music uses two conductor's bamboo clappers, six guan pipes, four di, two sheng, two cloud gongs, one processional welcome drum, and one clapper board.
translations.idiomatic: Processional Welcome Music employs two conductor's bamboo clappers, six guan pipes, four di, two sheng, two cloud gongs, one processional welcome drum, and one clapper board.

sentences.zh: 笙、笛同中和韶樂，戲竹、雲鑼、管、板同丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Sheng and di are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music; conductor's bamboo clappers, cloud gongs, guan pipes, and clapper boards are the same as in Danbi Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: The sheng and di match Zhonghe Shao Music; the conductor's bamboo clappers, cloud gongs, guan pipes, and clapper boards match Danbi Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 導迎鼓，制如大鼓而小，面徑二尺四分八釐，匡高一尺六寸二分。

translations.literal: The processional welcome drum is constructed like the large drum but smaller; face diameter two chi four fen eight li; frame height one chi six cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: The processional welcome drum follows the large drum's design but smaller—the head two chi, four fen, and eight li in diameter, the frame one chi, six cun, and two fen high.

sentences.zh: 繪五采雲龍，腹施銅膽。

translations.literal: Painted with five-colored cloud-and-dragon patterns; a copper resonator is fitted on the belly.
translations.idiomatic: It is painted with five-colored cloud-and-dragon designs, with a copper resonator mounted on the drum belly.

sentences.zh: 旁施金鐶四，系黃絨紃。

translations.literal: Four golden rings are fitted on the sides; yellow velvet cords are attached.
translations.idiomatic: Four gilt rings adorn the sides, tied with yellow velvet cords.

sentences.zh: 二人舁行，擊以硃槌。

translations.literal: Two men carry it while walking; struck with a vermilion mallet.
translations.idiomatic: Two bearers carry it in procession; it is struck with a vermilion mallet.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌鼓吹用龍鼓四十八，畫角二十四，大銅角八，小銅角八，金二，鉦四，笛十二，杖鼓四，拍板四。

translations.literal: Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music uses forty-eight dragon drums, twenty-four painted horns, eight large copper horns, eight small copper horns, two jin, four zheng, twelve di, four stick drums, four clapper boards.
translations.idiomatic: Nao song drum-and-pipe music employs forty-eight dragon drums, twenty-four painted horns, eight large and eight small copper horns, two jin, four zheng, twelve di, four stick drums, and four clapper boards.

sentences.zh: 笛同中和韶樂，板同丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Di are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music; clapper boards are the same as in Danbi Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: The di match Zhonghe Shao Music; the clapper boards match Danbi Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 龍鼓，木匡冒革，面徑一尺五寸三分六釐，匡高六寸四分八釐。

translations.literal: Dragon drums have wooden frames covered with hide; face diameter one chi five cun three fen six li; frame height six cun four fen eight li.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon drums have wooden frames covered with hide—the head one chi, five cun, three fen, and six li in diameter, the frame six cun, four fen, and eight li high.

sentences.zh: 面匡繪飾金鐶俱如導迎鼓。

translations.literal: The painted ornamentation on face and frame and the golden rings are all as on the processional welcome drum.
translations.idiomatic: The head, frame, painted decoration, and gilt rings all follow the processional welcome drum.

sentences.zh: 鐶系黃絨紃，行則懸於項，陳則置於架。

translations.literal: Rings are tied with yellow velvet cords; when marching they are hung at the neck, when deployed they are placed on stands.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow velvet cords attach to the rings; on the march the drum hangs from the neck, when stationed it rests on a stand.

sentences.zh: 架攢竹三，貫以樞而搘之。

translations.literal: The stand bundles three bamboos, pierced with a pivot to support it.
translations.idiomatic: The stand is three bamboo poles joined by a pivot pin for support.

sentences.zh: 畫角，木質，中虛腹廣，兩端銳。

translations.literal: Painted horns are of wood; hollow within, broad in the belly, sharp at both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Painted horns are wooden—hollow-bodied, wide in the middle, and tapered to sharp points at both ends.

sentences.zh: 長五尺四寸六分一釐二豪，上下束以銅，中束以藤五就，魨以漆。

translations.literal: Length five chi four cun six fen one li two hao; bound above and below with copper, the middle bound with rattan in five turns, coated with lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: It measures five chi, four cun, six fen, one li, and two hao long—bound with copper at top and bottom, wrapped five times with rattan at the middle, and lacquered throughout.

sentences.zh: 以木哨入角端吹之，哨長七寸二分九釐。

translations.literal: A wooden mouthpiece is inserted into the horn end to blow it; the mouthpiece is seven cun two fen nine li long.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden mouthpiece is fitted into the horn end for blowing; the mouthpiece is seven cun, two fen, and nine li long.

sentences.zh: 大銅角，一名大號，范銅為之，上下二截，形如竹筒，本細末大，中為圓球。

translations.literal: Large copper horns, also called large hao, are cast from copper in upper and lower sections; shaped like a bamboo tube, narrow at the base and wide at the tip, with a round bulb in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: The large copper horn—also called the large hao—is cast in copper in two telescoping sections like a bamboo tube, narrow at the base and flared at the mouth, with a round bulb at the center.

sentences.zh: 納上截於下截，用則引而伸之，通長三尺六寸七分二釐。

translations.literal: The upper section fits into the lower; when in use it is drawn out and extended; total extended length three chi six cun seven fen two li.
translations.idiomatic: The upper section slides into the lower and is pulled out for use; fully extended, it measures three chi, six cun, seven fen, and two li.

sentences.zh: 小銅角，一名二號，范銅為之，上下二截。

translations.literal: Small copper horns, also called second hao, are cast from copper in upper and lower sections.
translations.idiomatic: The small copper horn—also called the second hao—is cast in copper in two sections.

sentences.zh: 上截直，下截哆，各有圓球相銜，引納如大銅角，通長四尺一寸四釐。

translations.literal: The upper section is straight, the lower section flared; each has a round bulb interlocking; drawn and fitted like the large copper horn; total extended length four chi one cun four li.
translations.idiomatic: The upper section is straight and the lower flared; interlocking round bulbs join the two parts, which slide together like the large copper horn; extended length is four chi, one cun, and four li.

sentences.zh: 大角體巨聲下，小角體細聲高，不以長短論。

translations.literal: The large horn has a massive body and low tone; the small horn has a slender body and high tone; length is not the determining factor.
translations.idiomatic: The large horn is bulky with a low pitch; the small horn is slender with a high pitch—size, not length, determines the tone.

sentences.zh: 金，范銅為之。

translations.literal: Jin are cast from copper.
translations.idiomatic: The jin is cast in copper.

sentences.zh: 面平，徑一尺四寸五分八釐，深二寸二分七釐五豪。

translations.literal: The face is flat; diameter one chi four cun five fen eight li; depth two cun two fen seven li five hao.
translations.idiomatic: It has a flat face one chi, four cun, five fen, and eight li in diameter, and is two cun, two fen, seven li, and five hao deep.

sentences.zh: 旁穿二孔，結黃絨紃貫於木柄，提而擊之。

translations.literal: Two holes are pierced at the sides; yellow velvet cords are knotted and threaded through a wooden handle; lifted and struck.
translations.idiomatic: Two side holes take yellow velvet cords looped through a wooden handle; the player lifts it and strikes.

sentences.zh: 鉦，范銅為之，形如槃。

translations.literal: Zheng are cast from copper; shaped like a tray.
translations.idiomatic: The zheng is cast in copper, tray-shaped.

sentences.zh: 面平，口徑八寸六分四釐，深一寸二分九釐八豪，邊闊八分六釐四豪。

translations.literal: The face is flat; mouth diameter eight cun six fen four li; depth one cun two fen nine li eight hao; rim width eight fen six li four hao.
translations.idiomatic: The face is flat, the mouth eight cun, six fen, and four li across, the depth one cun, two fen, nine li, and eight hao, the rim eight fen, six li, and four hao wide.

sentences.zh: 穿六孔，兩兩相比，周以木匡，亦穿孔，以黃絨紃聯屬之。

translations.literal: Six holes are pierced, paired two by two; encircled with a wooden frame that is also pierced; linked together with yellow velvet cords.
translations.idiomatic: Six holes are drilled in opposing pairs; a wooden frame encircles the zheng and is pierced as well, and yellow velvet cords link the sets together.

sentences.zh: 左右銅鐶二，系黃絨紃，懸於項而擊之。

translations.literal: Two copper rings left and right; yellow velvet cords attached; hung at the neck and struck.
translations.idiomatic: Two copper rings on either side take yellow velvet cords; hung from the neck, they are struck in play.

sentences.zh: 杖鼓，同丹陛大樂，惟面繪流雲，中為太極。

translations.literal: Stick drums are the same as in Danbi Grand Music, except the face is painted with flowing clouds with the Great Ultimate at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Stick drums follow Danbi Grand Music, except the head is painted with flowing clouds surrounding a Taiji symbol at the center.

sentences.zh: 前部大樂，用大銅角四，小銅角四，金口角四。

translations.literal: Vanguard Grand Music uses four large copper horns, four small copper horns, four gold-mouthed horns.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Grand Music employs four large copper horns, four small copper horns, and four gold-mouthed horns.

sentences.zh: 大銅角、小銅角制同鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: Large and small copper horns are constructed the same as in Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music.
translations.idiomatic: Large and small copper horns follow the nao song drum-and-pipe design.

sentences.zh: 金口角，舊名瑣，木管，兩端金口，上弇下哆。

translations.literal: Gold-mouthed horns, formerly called suo, are wooden tubes with gilt mouths at both ends, constricted above and flared below.
translations.idiomatic: The gold-mouthed horn—formerly called the suo—is a wooden tube with gilt bell ends, narrow at the top and flared at the bottom.

sentences.zh: 管長九寸八分九釐。

translations.literal: The tube is nine cun eight fen nine li long.
translations.idiomatic: The tube is nine cun, eight fen, and nine li long.

sentences.zh: 管上金口長二寸一分六釐，為壺盧形，加小銅槃二。

translations.literal: The upper gilt mouth is two cun one fen six li long, gourd-shaped, with two small copper trays added.
translations.idiomatic: The upper gilt mouthpiece, two cun, one fen, and six li long, is shaped like a gourd and fitted with two small copper discs.

sentences.zh: 管下金口長四寸八分六釐，刻管如竹節相間，前七孔，後一孔，以蘆哨入管端吹之。

translations.literal: The lower gilt mouth is four cun eight fen six li long, the tube carved like bamboo nodes at intervals; seven holes in front, one hole in back; a reed mouthpiece is inserted into the tube end to blow it.
translations.idiomatic: The lower gilt mouth, four cun, eight fen, and six li long, is carved with bamboo-joint markings; seven finger holes face forward and one faces back; a reed whistle is inserted at the tube end for blowing.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌大樂，用金口角八，銅鼓二，銅點一，金一，鈸一，行鼓一。

translations.literal: Nao Song Grand Music uses eight gold-mouthed horns, two copper drums, one copper dot, one jin, one cymbal, one marching drum.
translations.idiomatic: Nao Song Grand Music calls for eight gold-mouthed horns, two copper drums, one copper dot, one jin, one cymbal, and one marching drum.

sentences.zh: 金口角同前部大樂，金同鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: Gold-mouthed horns are the same as in Vanguard Grand Music; jin are the same as in Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-mouthed horns match Vanguard Grand Music; the jin matches nao song drum-and-pipe music.

sentences.zh: 銅鼓，范銅為之，形如金，面徑九寸七分二釐，中隆起八分一釐，徑二寸六分七釐三豪。

translations.literal: Copper drums are cast from copper, shaped like jin; face diameter nine cun seven fen two li; the center rises eight fen one li, diameter two cun six fen seven li three hao.
translations.idiomatic: The copper drum is cast in copper, jin-shaped—the face nine cun, seven fen, and two li in diameter, with a central boss eight fen and one li high, two cun, six fen, seven li, and three hao across.

sentences.zh: 邊穿孔二，以黃絨紃懸而擊之。

translations.literal: Two holes are pierced at the rim; suspended with yellow velvet cords and struck.
translations.idiomatic: Two rim holes take yellow velvet cords for suspension; it is struck in play.

sentences.zh: 銅點，制如銅鼓而小。

translations.literal: Copper dots are constructed like copper drums but smaller.
translations.idiomatic: Copper dots follow the copper drum design but smaller.

sentences.zh: 鈸，范銅為之，面徑六寸四分八釐，中隆起一寸二分九釐六豪，徑三寸二分四釐。

translations.literal: Cymbals are cast from copper; face diameter six cun four fen eight li; the center rises one cun two fen nine li six hao, diameter three cun two fen four li.
translations.idiomatic: Cymbals are cast in copper—the face six cun, four fen, and eight li in diameter, with a central boss one cun, two fen, nine li, and six hao high, three cun, two fen, and four li across.

sentences.zh: 穿孔貫紃，左右合擊以和樂。

translations.literal: Holes are pierced and cords threaded through; struck together left and right to harmonize the music.
translations.idiomatic: Cords pass through pierced holes; the pair is clashed together to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: 行鼓，一名紘羅鼓。

translations.literal: Marching drums, also called hongluo drums.
translations.idiomatic: The marching drum is also called the hongluo drum.

sentences.zh: 木匡冒革，上大下小，面匡繪飾如龍鼓。

translations.literal: Wooden frame covered with hide, large above and small below; face and frame painted and ornamented like dragon drums.
translations.idiomatic: It has a wooden frame covered with hide, larger at the top and smaller below; head and frame are painted and decorated like the dragon drum.

sentences.zh: 金鐶四，貫以黃絨紃。

translations.literal: Four golden rings, threaded with yellow velvet cords.
translations.idiomatic: Four gilt rings are strung with yellow velvet cords.

sentences.zh: 行則跨於馬上，陳則置於架。

translations.literal: When marching they are straddled on horseback; when deployed they are placed on stands.
translations.idiomatic: On the march it is carried strapped across the saddle; when stationed it rests on a stand.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌清樂，用雲鑼二，笛二，平笛二，管二，笙二，金一，鈸一，銅點一，行鼓一。

translations.literal: Nao Song Qing Music uses two cloud gongs, two di, two level di, two guan pipes, two sheng, one jin, one cymbal, one copper dot, one marching drum.
translations.idiomatic: Nao Song Qing Music employs two cloud gongs, two di, two level di, two guan pipes, two sheng, one jin, one cymbal, one copper dot, and one marching drum.

sentences.zh: 笛、笙同中和韶樂，雲鑼、管同丹陛大樂，金同鐃歌鼓吹，鈸、銅點、行鼓同鐃歌大樂。

translations.literal: Di and sheng are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music; cloud gongs and guan pipes are the same as in Danbi Grand Music; jin are the same as in Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music; cymbals, copper dots, and marching drums are the same as in Nao Song Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: The di and sheng match Zhonghe Shao Music; cloud gongs and guan pipes match Danbi Grand Music; the jin matches nao song drum-and-pipe music; cymbals, copper dots, and marching drums match Nao Song Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 平笛，同中和韶樂，惟不加龍首尾。

translations.literal: Level di are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music, except dragon head and tail are not added.
translations.idiomatic: Level di follow Zhonghe Shao Music but without the dragon head and tail ornamentation.

sentences.zh: 行幸樂，合鐃歌大樂、鐃歌清樂之數，益以大銅角八，小銅角八，蒙古角二。

translations.literal: Travel Music combines the numbers of Nao Song Grand Music and Nao Song Qing Music, adding eight large copper horns, eight small copper horns, two Mongol horns.
translations.idiomatic: Travel music combines the instrument counts of Nao Song Grand and Qing Music, plus eight large copper horns, eight small copper horns, and two Mongol horns.

sentences.zh: 大銅角、小銅角同鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: Large and small copper horns are the same as in Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music.
translations.idiomatic: Large and small copper horns match nao song drum-and-pipe music.

sentences.zh: 蒙古角，一名蒙古號，木質，中虛末哆，上下二截。

translations.literal: Mongol horns, also called Mongol hao, are of wood; hollow within, flared at the tip, upper and lower sections.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol horn—also called the Mongol hao—is wooden, hollow-bodied, and flared at the mouth, in two sections.

sentences.zh: 角有雌雄二制，雄角上口內徑三分四釐五豪，雌角上口內徑二分八釐五豪，皆於管端施銅口，以角哨納入吹之。

translations.literal: Horns come in male and female forms; the male horn's upper mouth inner diameter is three fen four li five hao, the female horn's upper mouth inner diameter two fen eight li five hao; both have gilt mouths fitted at the tube end, with a horn mouthpiece inserted to blow.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol horns come in male and female types—the male's upper bore is three fen, four li, and five hao across, the female's two fen, eight li, and five hao; both take a gilt mouth at the tube end and a horn whistle for blowing.

sentences.zh: 雄者聲濁，雌者聲清。

translations.literal: The male sounds thick, the female clear.
translations.idiomatic: The male horn produces a low, thick tone; the female a clear, high one.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌用大銅角四，小銅角四，金口角八，金四，鑼二，銅鼓二，鐃四，鈸四，小和鈸二，花匡鼓四，得勝鼓四，海笛四，雲鑼四，簫六，笛六，管六，篪六，笙六。

translations.literal: Nao Song uses four large copper horns, four small copper horns, eight gold-mouthed horns, four jin, two gongs, two copper drums, four naos, four cymbals, two small harmony cymbals, four flower-frame drums, four victory drums, four sea flutes, four cloud gongs, six xiao, six di, six guan pipes, six chi, six sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Nao song music calls for four large and four small copper horns, eight gold-mouthed horns, four jin, two gongs, two copper drums, four naos, four cymbals, two small harmony cymbals, four flower-frame drums, four victory drums, four sea flutes, four cloud gongs, six xiao, six di, six guan pipes, six chi, and six sheng.

sentences.zh: 大銅角、小銅角、金同鐃歌鼓吹，金口角同前部大樂，銅鼓、鈸同鐃歌大樂，簫、笛、篪、笙同中和韶樂，雲鑼、管同丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Large and small copper horns and jin are the same as in Nao Song Drum-and-Pipe Music; gold-mouthed horns are the same as in Vanguard Grand Music; copper drums and cymbals are the same as in Nao Song Grand Music; xiao, di, chi, and sheng are the same as in Zhonghe Shao Music; cloud gongs and guan pipes are the same as in Danbi Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Large and small copper horns and the jin match nao song drum-and-pipe music; gold-mouthed horns match Vanguard Grand Music; copper drums and cymbals match Nao Song Grand Music; xiao, di, chi, and sheng match Zhonghe Shao Music; cloud gongs and guan pipes match Danbi Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 鑼，制同銅鼓而厚，聲較銅鼓低小。

translations.literal: Gongs are constructed like copper drums but thicker; the sound is lower and smaller than copper drums.
translations.idiomatic: Gongs follow the copper drum design but are thicker, producing a lower, softer tone than copper drums.

sentences.zh: 鐃，范銅為之，面徑一尺二寸。

translations.literal: Naos are cast from copper; face diameter one chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Naos are cast in copper with a face one chi and two cun in diameter.

sentences.zh: 中隆起，穿孔貫紃，左右合擊。

translations.literal: The center rises; holes are pierced and cords threaded through; struck together left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The center is domed; cords pass through pierced holes, and the pair is clashed together.
